full_description: Two named objects (A the mover, B the reference) and 1-3 distractors are on the table. The instruction tells the robot to pick up A and place it in a spatial relation to B: 'beside' (next to, on the table) or 'on top of' (stacked onto B). Tests spatial-relation understanding: the SAME scene admits either relation, so the relation word alone decides the correct placement.
schema: {A}=the mover object (picked up), filled by play_once with the literal 'the {color} {noun}' (no '/', so replace_placeholders substitutes verbatim -> color+noun controlled). The reference object uses a DIFFERENT key per relation so RoboTwin's filter_instructions routes templates by relation: beside uses {B}, on-top uses {C} (the env sets info['info'] with {B} XOR {C}). {a}=arm. beside frames = move_can_pot native pool with mover/ref swapped ({A}<->{B}); on-top frames = same single-arm structure with on-top prepositions (stack_blocks_two vocabulary). Color is a grounding aid, not a scored axis; the scored axis is the spatial relation.
preference: beside borrowed verbatim from move_can_pot (swapped); on-top authored in the same style. num of words should not exceed 12.
